Render a change table to HTML or PDF

Source: R/yoyh.R
yoyhtml.Rd

yoyhtml() writes one self-contained HTML page (every style inlined, nothing fetched, so the file renders the same years later): the table, a card per series with its change over the span (yoysmry()) and the notes. yoypdf() writes a PDF of the table, paginated when it does not fit, with the standard Helvetica font and no other program: crimlab writes the file itself.

Usage

yoyhtml(
  x,
  file,
  title = "Year-over-year change",
  sub = "",
  pal = "diverging",
  better = "neutral",
  digits = 1L,
  bars = TRUE,
  intv = TRUE,
  notes = NULL,
  lag = 1
)

yoypdf(
  x,
  file,
  title = "Year-over-year change",
  sub = "",
  pal = "diverging",
  better = "neutral",
  digits = 1L,
  intv = TRUE,
  notes = NULL,
  width = 11,
  height = 8.5,
  lag = 1
)

Arguments

x

A change table (yoypx()).

file

The file path. A name with no suffix is given the format's own (.html, .pdf).

title

The heading (and the page title).

sub

The line under the heading.

pal

The palette: "diverging", "safe" or "mono".

better

Which direction is better: "neutral", "higher" or "lower".

digits

The decimals of the change shown.

bars

TRUE draws a bar under each change, proportional to its size.

intv

TRUE shows the interval column of a count table.

notes

NULL, or footnotes.

lag

The periods per step of the table, for the summary and the note on the first periods.

width, height

The PDF page in inches, each from 2 to 200.

Value

The path written, invisibly.

Details

Colour encodes the direction of an improvement, not the sign of the change: with better = "lower" (fewer assaults, fewer days in segregation) a rise is drawn in the colour for worse, with "higher" (a completion rate) in the colour for better, and with "neutral" (the default) every change in the neutral colour. The palette "safe" (blue and orange) stays apart in the common forms of colour blindness; "mono" is for print. The first period of each series, with nothing to compare with, is said once under the table rather than on every first row. The PDF holds ASCII only: dashes and arrows become - and +, other characters their transliteration (toascii()).

See also

yoywr(), yoycsv().

Examples

# simulated police-reported counts by offence and year, any agency
d <- data.frame(year = rep(2021:2023, 2),
                offence = rep(c("Assault", "Robbery"), each = 3),
                n = c(812, 845, 790, 120, 131, 98))
y <- yoypx(d$n, d$year, d$offence)
f <- tempfile(fileext = ".html")
yoyhtml(y, f, title = "Reported offences (simulated)", better = "lower")
g <- tempfile(fileext = ".pdf")
yoypdf(y, g, title = "Reported offences (simulated)")
# simulated days in segregation by fiscal year
s <- yoylbl(yoypx(c(4100, 3900, 4400), 2021:2023), fylbl)
yoyhtml(s, f, title = "Days in segregation (simulated)", better = "lower")
unlink(c(f, g))
